description: Killing parrots crashes your game. Note: I did kill other mobs and it isn t just swinging the sword and i got the same result everytime i killed a parrot. 19w40a: [^crash-2019-10-03_20.30.29-client.txt] Description: Unexpected error java.lang.NullPointerException: Unexpected error at atd.a(SourceFile:407) at axx.f(SourceFile:1234) at dmq.a(SourceFile:363) at das.aE(SourceFile:1234) at das.aG(SourceFile:1517) at das.n(SourceFile:1367) at das.d(SourceFile:907) at das.b(SourceFile:569) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition 19w40a.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Summon a parrot using the command: `/summon minecraft:parrot ~ ~ ~`.
4. Attack the parrot.
5. Observe that the game crashes with a java.lang.NullPointerException error.
Observed Behavior: When attacking a parrot in the game, a java.lang.NullPointerException occurs, resulting in a crash that disrupts gameplay. This issue consistently arises every time a parrot is killed, regardless of the method used for the attack, as the player has confirmed that other mobs can be killed without causing a crash. The error message indicates that the exception is thrown from a specific source file within the game’s code, specifically at line 407 in the atd class and continues through several other classes, ultimately leading to the main method in the net.minecraft.client.main.Main class. The player is using version 19w40a, and the crash log associated with this issue has been documented for further analysis. This bug seems to be isolated to parrots and does not affect other mobs, suggesting a potential problem with the way the game handles the parrot entity upon being attacked.
Expected Behavior: When a player attacks a parrot, the expected behavior is that the parrot should be damaged without causing any game crashes or errors. After the attack, the parrot should either be defeated or remain alive, allowing for continued interaction without any interruptions. The game should handle the event smoothly, ensuring that no NullPointerException occurs, thus providing a stable gaming experience in Java Edition 19w40a.
